description: An AI pipeline re-ran published Wiley papers from their public data and checked every headline number against pre-registered tolerances.
footer: Straive innovation prototype. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Wiley. Articles are used under CC BY; datasets are linked, not mirrored.

hero.kicker: Reproducibility audit · Wiley open-access papers · prototype
hero.title: Do Wiley papers reproduce?
hero.lead: We took {n_papers} open-access Wiley papers, downloaded their public data, and re-ran the analyses without the authors' help. Every headline number was compared against a tolerance we committed to git before running anything.

chart_heading: Most numbers land close. A few don't, and the reasons are specific.
chart_sub: Each row is one headline claim. The dot shows how far our value is from the paper's, counted in units of the last digit the paper printed: for a printed 0.42, a unit is 0.01. The green band is the tolerance fixed in git before we ran anything; by default it is half a unit, so 'Reproduced' means our number rounds to the paper's.
chart_caption: Colour is the verdict, not the distance: a dot can sit close to zero and still be 'Not reproduced' when the significance conclusion flips. The axis is logarithmic beyond one unit so small and large misses fit on one scale. Hover or focus a row for both values, the tolerance and the relative difference. {n_not_reproducible} claims could not be computed from the deposited data.
narrative: Reproducibility is not a yes-or-no property of a paper. Within a single paper, some numbers came back to the last printed digit and others did not. The useful output is the claim-level table, not a badge.

When a number misses, the paper usually tells you why, if you read closely. In the papers that did not fully reproduce, the reviewers found inconsistencies inside the papers themselves: sample sizes printed differently in different places, standard errors that cannot produce the printed p-values, and Discussion sections that contradict their own tables. These are exactly the signals an editor would want before publication.

The method is the product, not the verdict count. {n_papers} papers is not a rate, and we picked papers we expected to be tractable. What carries over is the pipeline: claims frozen in git before analysis, scripted re-runs from the original repositories, and an independent auditor who re-ran everything from a clean checkout.
screening_heading: Finding reproducible papers is itself a signal
methods: Screen. Search Europe PMC for open-access Wiley papers, read each data availability statement, and check the article licence (CC BY only), the data licence and a real anonymous download.

Pre-register. An extractor agent reads the full text and writes claims.json: each headline number exactly as printed, its location, the method steps, the ambiguities and a tolerance. The lead commits it and tags it claims-frozen-<paper> before any analysis runs.

Reproduce. A separate agent runs the authors' code unchanged where it exists, otherwise writes one clean script from the methods. The script itself writes results.json. Every assumption is logged before results are seen; any later change is marked POST-HOC.
Compare. compare.py applies fixed rules (below) to the frozen claims and the script's output. No human or agent picks the verdict.

Audit. A fresh agent that saw none of the above clones the repository, re-downloads the data from the original source, checks the checksums, re-runs the script three times, cross-checks key numbers with a different implementation, and can override a verdict only with a written reason.
Package. Each audited claim becomes an evaluation task in the CORE-Bench format, with a PaperBench-style rubric, for AI-lab evaluation sets.

verdict_rules.Reproduced: Our value is within the pre-registered tolerance of the paper's printed value.
verdict_rules.Partial: Outside tolerance, but the same direction, the same significance conclusion and within half the paper's magnitude.
verdict_rules.Not reproduced: Computed, but the direction, the significance conclusion or the magnitude differs beyond that.
verdict_rules.Not reproducible: The value could not be computed from the deposited data and the stated methods.

cam4-2024-hpd.finding: Every headline estimate of the meta-analysis came back to the printed digit. The confidence intervals and p-values in the paper's own Table do not agree with each other, so we graded point estimates.
cam4-2024-hpd.teaser: All headline estimates reproduce to the printed digit.

ee-2022-roedeer-sexratio.finding: The core sex-ratio result reproduces. The climate model does not: neither temperature term is significant when re-run, and the paper prints three different sample sizes.
ee-2022-roedeer-sexratio.teaser: Sex ratio holds; the climate effect does not.

hsr-2023-ei-happiness.finding: Directions match for most predictors, but magnitudes drift and the age effect reverses sign. The paper's own Discussion also contradicts its table on age.
hsr-2023-ei-happiness.teaser: Directions mostly hold; the age effect flips.

audit.cam4-2024-hpd: A separate agent re-downloaded the data, re-ran the script three times with identical results, and recomputed the estimates by an independent route (direct GLMM and the meta package). It agreed with every verdict. It noted that the paper's Table uses z-based intervals while our script uses t-based ones (only intervals and p-values differ), and that the paper's tumour-type intervals match no standard test.
audit.ee-2022-roedeer-sexratio: A separate agent re-ran everything three times with identical results and recomputed every claim in Python to five or more decimals. It agreed with every verdict. It found that the data give exactly the sample size printed in the paper's Tables when no year filter is applied, so the different number in the Abstract is probably a transposition.
audit.hsr-2023-ei-happiness: A separate agent re-ran the script three times with identical results and refitted the model in Python, matching to six decimals. It agreed with every verdict and flagged that the women-versus-men claim fails only narrowly on significance. It also found that one happiness item correlates negatively with the rest of the scale, which suggests a scoring problem in the deposited total.

task_example.heading: What an AI lab gets
task_example.intro: Every audited claim becomes an evaluation task with a known answer: {n_tasks} so far. The format follows CORE-Bench, with a PaperBench-style rubric. Where the paper's printed number does not reproduce, the ground truth is the independently re-run value, so an agent that copies the paper fails. This is the task for the reversed age effect.

footnotes: Papers were chosen for tractability (open data, CC BY licence, analysis runnable in R or Python in under an hour), so these results do not estimate a reproducibility rate for any journal.
Dryad, the most common data repository for Wiley ecology papers, blocks anonymous file downloads (HTTP 401) as of 20 October 2026. Machine access needs an API token.
Verdicts are produced by scripts/compare.py; its rules and unit tests were committed before any reproduction ran.
Article text was retrieved as JATS XML from Europe PMC. Wiley Online Library blocks scripted access.

Prior art: CODECHECK, ReScience C, the Institute for Replication, the Odum Institute (AJPS) and SEER-Repro (arXiv 2610.23845) have reproduced some Wiley papers. None covers Wiley's ecology and health portfolio systematically. See landscape.md.

Limitation we found in our own process: the claims freeze is verifiable in git, but the reproducers' statement that each assumption was logged before results were seen is self-reported (code, log and outputs were committed together). The next version commits the analysis plan before the first run.
